questions.q: Why does the report need to be published to the Power BI Service rather than just shared as a .pbix file?
options: The stakeholder doesn't have Power BI Desktop and shouldn't need it; the Service lets the report be opened in a browser
A .pbix file cannot contain DAX measures once saved
The Power BI Service is required before any slicer can function
Power BI Desktop files expire 24 hours after being saved
questions.explain: Desktop is the build tool; the Power BI Service is where a finished report is actually delivered to someone who just needs to view it in a browser.

questions.q: Why is 'My Workspace' the wrong publishing destination for this project's final deliverable?
options: My Workspace has a maximum file size smaller than this report
Reports published to My Workspace cannot include slicers
My Workspace isn't shareable with other people, so the stakeholder couldn't access the report there
My Workspace cannot store datasets with DAX measures
questions.explain: The lesson recommends a shared workspace instead, since My Workspace is appropriate only for personal testing, not for handing a report to a stakeholder.

questions.q: What is the key difference between the 'dataset' and the 'report' once published to the Power BI Service?
options: The report can be refreshed on a schedule; the dataset cannot
The dataset is only visible to admins; the report is visible to everyone
The dataset holds the data model, relationships, and measures (and has its own refresh settings); the report holds the pages and visuals a viewer sees
They are two names for the exact same object with no functional difference
questions.explain: Publishing a .pbix file creates two related but separate objects in the workspace; refresh settings specifically live on the dataset, not the report.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend direct sharing with the stakeholder's email rather than building a full Power BI App?
options: A full App is scoped for multiple reports and multiple audiences, which is over-engineering for a single stakeholder's one-report request
Power BI Apps cannot contain reports built with a native SQL query
Apps require a separate Power BI license tier that Carraway doesn't have
Sharing by email is the only sharing method Power BI supports
questions.explain: Matching delivery effort to the actual scope (one stakeholder, one report) means direct sharing is the right call, not a packaged App meant for broader distribution.

questions.q: What access does the stakeholder need for the Share link to open the report directly, rather than an access request screen?
options: A separate Power BI Desktop license installed on their machine
Edit access to the underlying dataset
At least Viewer access to the workspace (or access granted through the share dialog)
Admin access to the entire Power BI tenant
questions.explain: Confirming Viewer-level access (via the workspace or the share dialog itself) ensures the shared link opens the report instead of prompting for access.
